newsitem.title: FRANCE: Experts to meet this week over N. Caledonia mines.
newsitem.headline: Experts to meet this week over N. Caledonia mines.

text.p: The legal experts of Societe Miniere de Sud Pacifique (SMSP) and of French nickel group Eramet are expected to meet this week to discuss plans by the two companies to swap mining titles in New Caledonia, Eramet said on Wednesday.
"We are trying to set up a meeting this week between our legal experts and those of SMSP," an Eramet spokesman told Reuters.
A second meeting between the mining experts of SMSP, Canadian group Falconbridge and Eramet, may also take place in early June, he said.

The planned exchange involves Eramet's Koniambo field and SMSP's Poum field. The nickel extracted from Koniambo would be used to supply a smelter that SMSP, a company controlled by Kanak nationalists, and Falconbridge plan to build in the north of the French territory.

On May 2, the presidents of Eramet, Falconbridge and SMSP met to review the plan and agreed legal experts would be brought in to discuss the legal, technical and financial problems identified during the meeting.
One main issue to settle is the amount and the terms of the financial compensation that must be paid to Eramet as a result of the exchange, the spokesman said.
The government, which controls 55 percent of Eramet, is backing the construction of the new smelter as part of a plan to appease local separatists ahead of a 1998 referendum on independence.

It has threatened to take control of Eramet's board at the next annual shareholders' meeting and to replace chairman Yves Rambaud, who has opposed any plans that would curb the group's development in New Caledonia.
On Tuesday Eramet said it had postponed the annual general meeting called for May 29 to give itself more time to consider a number of requests put forward by shareholders and staff.
Staff representatives want employees to be given the chance to select three directors from their own ranks.
Institutional investors have put forward proposals aimed at insuring the future independence of Eramet's board, the spokesman said.
A new date for the meeting will be set by the board which is due to meet "probably within two weeks", he said.
